title: Text 2
subtitle: 数字隐私之争：警方查看嫌疑人手机数据

sentences.en: Just how much does the Constitution protect your digital data?
sentences.zh: 宪法到底能在多大程度上保护你的数字数据？

sentences.en: The Supreme Court will now consider whether police can search the contents of a mobile phone without a warrant if the phone is on or around a person during an arrest.
sentences.zh: 最高法院现在将审议，如果逮捕某人时手机就在其身上或身边，警方是否可以不经搜查令就检查手机内容。

sentences.en: California has asked the justices to refrain from a sweeping ruling, particularly one that upsets the old assumption that authorities may search through the possessions of suspects at the time of their arrest.
sentences.zh: 加州请求法官们不要作出过于笼统的裁决，尤其不要推翻旧的假设——当局在逮捕嫌疑人时可以搜查其随身物品。

sentences.en: It is hard, the state argues, for judges to assess the implications of new and rapidly changing technologies.
sentences.zh: 该州辩称，法官们很难评估日新月异的新技术所产生的影响。

sentences.en: The court would be recklessly modest if it followed California's advice.
sentences.zh: 如果最高法院听从加州的建议，那将是不负责任的过分谦逊。

sentences.en: Enough of the implications are discernable, even obvious, so that the justices can and should provide updated guidelines to police, lawyers and defendants.
sentences.zh: 这些影响中有很多是可辨别的，甚至显而易见，因此法官们能够而且应该为警方、律师和被告提供更新的指导方针。

sentences.en: They should start by discarding California's lame argument that exploring the contents of a smartphone — a vast storehouse of digital information — is similar to, say, going through a suspect's purse.
sentences.zh: 他们应当首先摒弃加州站不住脚的论点，即检查智能手机（数字信息的巨大宝库）的内容，与翻查嫌疑人的钱包等物品类似。

sentences.en: The court has ruled that police don't violate the Fourth Amendment when they go through the wallet or pocketbook of an arrestee without a warrant.
sentences.zh: 最高法院已裁定，警方在无搜查令的情况下翻查被逮捕者的钱包或手包，并不违反宪法第四修正案。

sentences.en: But exploring one's smartphone is more like entering his or her home.
sentences.zh: 但检查智能手机更像进入某人的家中。

sentences.en: A smartphone may contain an arrestee's reading history, financial history, medical history and comprehensive records of recent correspondence.
sentences.zh: 智能手机可能包含被逮捕者的阅读记录、财务记录、医疗记录以及近期的完整通讯记录。

sentences.en: The development of "cloud computing," meanwhile, has made that exploration so much the easier.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，“云计算”的发展使这种检查变得更为容易。

sentences.en: Americans should take steps to protect their digital privacy.
sentences.zh: 美国人应当采取措施保护自己的数字隐私。

sentences.en: But keeping sensitive information on these devices is increasingly a requirement of normal life.
sentences.zh: 但在这些设备上保存敏感信息正日益成为正常生活的需要。

sentences.en: Citizens still have a right to expect private documents to remain private and protected by the Constitution's prohibition on unreasonable searches.
sentences.zh: 公民仍然有权期待私人文件保持私密，并受到宪法禁止无理搜查条款的保护。

sentences.en: As so often is the case, stating that principle doesn't ease the challenge of line- drawing.
sentences.zh: 正如通常的情况一样，阐明这一原则并不能缓解划定界限的难题。

sentences.en: In many cases, it would not be overly burdensome for authorities to obtain a warrant to search through phone contents.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，当局为搜查手机内容而申请搜查令并不十分繁琐。

sentences.en: They could still invalidate Fourth Amendment protections when facing severe, urgent circumstances, and they could take reasonable measures to ensure that phone data are not erased or altered while waiting for a warrant.
sentences.zh: 在面临严重、紧急的情况时，他们仍可以搁置第四修正案的保护，并且可以在等待搜查令期间采取合理措施，确保手机数据不被删除或更改。

sentences.en: The court, though, may want to allow room for police to cite situations where they are entitled to more freedom.
sentences.zh: 不过，最高法院也许想为警方留下余地，以便他们援引有权获得更多自由的某些情形。

sentences.en: But the justices should not swallow California's argument whole.
sentences.zh: 但是，法官们不应全盘接受加州的论点。

sentences.en: New, disruptive technology sometimes demands novel applications of the Constitution's protections.
sentences.zh: 新的颠覆性技术有时要求对宪法的保护条款进行新颖的运用。

sentences.en: Orin Kerr, a law professor, compares the explosion and accessibility of digital information in the 21st century with the establishment of automobile use as a virtual necessity of life in the 20th: The justices had to specify novel rules for the new personal domain of the passenger car then; they must sort out how the Fourth Amendment applies to digital information now.
sentences.zh: 法学教授奥林·克尔把21世纪数字信息的爆炸式增长与便捷获取，比作20世纪汽车成为生活中不可或缺之物的确立过程：当时，法官们不得不为乘用车这一新兴的私人领域制定新的规则；如今，他们必须厘清第四修正案如何适用于数字信息。

questions.stem: The Supreme Court will work out whether, during an arrest, it is legitimate to ____

options.A: prevent suspects from deleting their phone contents.
options.B: search for suspects’ mobile phones without a warrant.
options.C: check suspects’ phone contents without being authorized.
options.D: prohibit suspects from using their mobile phones.

questions.analysis: 这是一道事实细节题，根据题干关键词The Supreme Court回文定位到第一段的第二句话，"The Supreme Court will now consider whether police can search for the contents of a mobile phone without a warrant if the phone is on or around a person during an arrest",一一比对选项，原文中的"police can search for the contents of a mobile phone without a warrant"与选项C "check suspects' phone contents without being authorized"是同义替换，其他选项均是无关选项。

questions.stem: The author’s attitude toward California’s argument is one of ____
questions.analysis: 本题是观点态度题，考察作者的态度。根据题干关键词"California's argument"，可以定位到文章第四段第一句"They should start by discarding California's lame argument…"。由第四段第一句话中的"discard（抛弃）"和"lame（没有说服力的）"可以看出作者对于California's argument 是不支持的态度，因此选A。

questions.stem: The author believes that exploring one’s phone contents is comparable to ____
questions.analysis: 根据题干关键词the author believes和"exploring one's phone contents is comparable to"可回文定位到文章第四段第三句"But exploring one's smartphone is more like entering his or her home"，选项A语义与之一致，其中，getting into与entering对应，one's residence与his or her home对应，故A选项为正确答案。

questions.stem: In Paragraphs 5 and 6, the author shows his concern that ____

options.A: principles are hard to be clearly expressed.
options.B: the court is giving police less room for action.
options.C: citizens’ privacy is not effectively protected.
options.D: phones are used to store sensitive information.

questions.analysis: 根据题干信息In paragraphs 5and 6定位第5段第一句话"Americans should take steps to protect their digital privacy.及第6段最后一句话，...and they could take reasonable measures to.....，可推知作者的顾虑，因此答案为C.

questions.stem: Orin Kerr’s comparison is quoted to indicate that ____

options.A: the Constitution should be implemented flexibly.
options.B: new technology requires reinterpretation of the Constitution.
options.C: California’s argument violates principles of the Constitution.
options.D: principles of the Constitution should never be altered.

questions.analysis: 这是一道例证题，根据题干关键词Orin Kerr可以回文定位到文章最后一段。作者引用Orin Kerr这个人的比较是为了说明相关的论点。分析最后一段结构可知，最后一段的第三句和第四句都是在阐述该例子本身，所以相关论点应该往前面找，即是第二句话，"New，disruptive technology sometimes demands novel applications of the Constitution's protection",选项A与之同义替换，其中，be implemented和applications对应，novel和flexibly对应。 Text 3
